result.note: A production log measures the flow passing each depth while the well flows; going up, it grows past each zone that produces. A share at a depth is the part of the pass's oil or water entering below that depth (1 at the bottom of the well's inflow, 0 above the top zone). comes_in_from_m to to_m holds 90% of each phase's inflow. Only shares are given: the files' rates have no units, and the plots' are downhole volumes. A plug set at a depth shuts off what enters below it: the shares below say what it could remove, not what it did; plugs_set gives what each plug already set did to the well (water cut and oil before and after). A bridge plug is set in blank pipe, never inside a perforated interval (inside_perforation_m names the interval a depth falls in; blank_pipe_m lists the gaps, and each pass's at_blank_pipe gives the shares below the top and the bottom of every gap: the depths a plug can actually be set at). A plug set after a survey (its plugs_set_since) already shut off what entered below it: on that log a depth or gap at or below it is already_isolated (a plug there cuts nothing new), and of_flow_left gives what a shallower plug would cut as a share of the flow left above the old plug. since_survey says how old the latest log is and how far the water cut has moved since: an old log may no longer show where the water enters, and a new one would settle it. Each survey's passes were run at several surface rates. A survey read off pictures carries the checks of that reading.
